200-about-english: Literature in English, drama (dramatic literature and performance), and cultural studies across visual and verbal media. Work in all three while concentrating on one. Those applying to Honours should see an Honours adviser throughout.
200-medieval-studies-minor-concentration: Interdisciplinary training in history, literature, art history, languages, religion and philosophy, useful for graduate study. Program Director: Prof. Cecily Hilsdale.
200-world-cinemas-minor-concentration: Courses across departments, mainly in Arts, on national and international cinema traditions and modes of production.
200-department-of-english-student-associ: Represents English students; taking any English course makes you a member.
200-admission-requirements-to-the-joint-: The Honours Committee decides on your program GPA, at least 3.50. Get the form online or at Arts 155. Allow several weeks, as incomplete applications aren't considered.

You submit a Program Course Proposal, and acceptance may depend on changes to it. Later substitutions must be approved by the Joint Honours adviser at the start of each term to graduate with Joint Honours.
200-location: McCall MacBain Arts Building, Room 155, 853 Sherbrooke St. W.
201-program-description: Can expand to the Major. See the English Department Handbook.
201-complementary-courses-12-credits: Topics courses change yearly and may count differently, so confirm with your adviser when registering.
201-additional-literature: 6 credits from Literature offerings. ENGL courses not on these lists, such as Cultural Studies, may not count.
202-drama-and-theatre-option-s-offerings: 6 credits from the option's lists, not required courses. Unlisted ones, such as Cultural Studies, may not count; ask an adviser.
202-drama-and-theatre-courses-of-interes: Normally 3 credits from other departments may count, with an adviser's signature on your audit sheet before taking them. Other Arts courses may qualify if the adviser sees the syllabus.
Graduation needs a complete signed audit sheet in Arts 155. Some courses are in other languages or have prerequisites.
203-additional-cultural-studies: 6 credits from the option's lists. Others, such as Literature courses, may not count.
204-program-description: Grounding in basic texts and methods and wide knowledge of the field.
204-required-courses-9-credits: Take them in your first two terms.
204-complementary-courses-27-credits: Confirm with your adviser which requirement a topics course meets that year.
204-theory-criticism-and-methods: 3 credits from the list or with adviser permission.
204-areas-of-english-literature: 3 credits each from two of: Backgrounds, Old English, Medieval, Renaissance.
204-areas-of-english-literature-2: 3 credits each from two of: Restoration, 18th Century, Romantic, Victorian, 19th Century American.
205-additional-courses: 6 credits from Literature, Cultural Studies, or Drama and Theatre; others need adviser approval.
206-program-description: Analysis of cultural expression and the media that spread it, sharpening analytical skills through critical approaches. Not journalism or communications, and no film or video production training.
207-other-departments: Normally 6 credits from other departments, or up to 9 with strong grounds and an adviser's advance signature.
207-program-description: Drama in social and philosophical context, as a liberal arts discipline. Not professional theatre training.
208-program-description: Apply normally after two terms in a Departmental program with 18+ English credits. Limited places. You also need a Minor.
CGPA 3.30 to apply; special permission from the Director is possible with CGPA 3.0–3.3 and program GPA 3.5, or CGPA 3.3 and program GPA 3.3–3.5.
Up to 9 credits outside with written approval, at least 6 at 500 level. The Honours Essay (ENGL 491D) is in your final year, planned with a supervisor when applying.
Honours: 54 credits, B+ on the essay, CGPA 3.00, program GPA 3.50. First Class: A, CGPA 3.50, program GPA 3.70.
208-required-courses-18-credits: ENGL 202, 203 and 311 in your first two terms; ENGL 360 in second year.
208-complementary-courses-36-credits: At least 6 at 500; up to 9 from another department with permission; at least 3 on a Major Author and 3 on Canadian Literature; at most 9 at 200, none in final year. Confirm topics courses with your adviser.
210-areas-of-english-literature: 3 credits each from two of: Early 20th Century, Modernist, Post-modernist, Contemporary.
211-required-courses-12-credits: Take ENGL 230 and 355 in your first two terms.
211-complementary-courses-42-credits: At least 6 at 500; up to 9 from another department with permission; at most 9 at 200, none in final year. Includes 3 credits of practice-based courses.
211-shakespeare-or-another-major-figure-: 3 credits on Shakespeare, or another major figure with the instructor's signed permission.
211-400-level-theory-courses: 3 credits with a theoretical component at 400+.
212-drama-and-theatre-courses-of-interes: Normally 6 credits from other departments, up to 9 on strong grounds with advance signature. Other Arts courses may qualify if your adviser approves the syllabus. A complete audit sheet in Arts 155 is needed to graduate.
213-required-courses-15-credits: ENGL 275, 277 and 359 in your first two terms.
213-complementary-courses-39-credits: At least 6 at 500; up to 9 from another department with permission; at most 9 at 200, none in final year. Confirm topics courses.
214-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline. Apply once you have 9–18 English credits, normally by the end of January or in mid-April; only those with over 18 credits by January apply in Fall.
CGPA 3.30 to apply, with the same special-permission routes as Honours. Forms at Arts 155.
Keep program GPA 3.50. Joint Honours: CGPA 3.00, program GPA 3.50, B+ on the essay. First Class: 3.50, 3.70 and A. A special adviser is named each year.
214-complementary-courses-24-credits: 6 credits at 400+ beyond Advanced Study, at least 3 on a Major Author, 3 more at 500, at most 9 at 200, none in final year. Confirm topics courses.
214-advanced-study: 6 credits: the honours essay, or else two 500-level courses chosen with advisers. Rarely, a third route if formally recommended for the joint subject, such as a joint essay with Anthropology.
215-areas-of-english-literature: 3 credits from one of: Backgrounds, Old English, Medieval, Renaissance.
215-areas-of-english-literature-2: 3 credits from one of: Restoration, 18th Century, Romantic, Victorian, 19th Century American.
217-complementary-courses-30-credits: 6 credits at 400+ beyond Advanced Study, 3 more at 500, at most 9 at 200, none in final year.
217-dramatic-literature: 3 credits; see the Department's site for this year's list.
218-complementary-courses-27-credits: 6 credits at 400+ beyond Advanced Study, 3 more at 500, at most 9 at 200, none in final year. Confirm topics courses.
219-program-description: Interdisciplinary training in history, literature, art history, languages, religion and philosophy, useful for graduate study.
219-complementary-courses-15-credits: Only 9 from any one department, and at most 6 below the 300 level.
